node_definition.done_when:
Measure whether the certificate forward map converges with cell count once its plasma support is right. The ladder prototype (scripts/prototypes/ladder/map.py; report /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/nova/resolution-pivot/proto-ladder.md; H200 job 1283109) found the following. The production map's diverted relative sup at the analytic state rises from 0.197327 at 550 cells to 0.361706 at 2,098, while the limited case holds 0.0012 at both. The support comes from ForwardFluxOperator._fixed_design_read (Topology.read_qualification), not from the new topology read. ForwardFluxOperator._support_partition (nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py near line 3308) calls _fixed_design_read unconditionally. The new read (nova.equilibrium.topology.read, TopologyPolicy defaults, closed-form analytic field) measured diverted saddle membership 2.74e-5 at 2,000 cells.

Done when:

(1) Support arms. In scripts/prototypes/support only, with no product module or public signature changed, the certificate map at the analytic state runs with three support arms through a private override of the support partition, in a prototype namespace, as scripts/prototypes/order2/read.py does:
- legacy: the production _fixed_design_read, the control;
- read: the support built from nova.equilibrium.topology.read on the closed-form analytic field, the ladder's arm A;
- exact: the support built from the analytic state's own flux and its true boundary level and X-point, the floor.
For each arm, the report states what quantity becomes the support (cell fractions, boundary flux, X-point) and how it enters current booking.

(2) Positive control. The legacy arm reproduces the ladder's 0.197327 at 550 diverted cells within 1e-9 relative.

(3) Rows. Limited and diverted, at about 550, 2,000 and 5,000 realised cells, for all three arms. Each row gives the realised count, the map relative sup and rms, the support membership error against the exact arm, the booked net current against the analytic net current, cold compile, warm execution, serialized executable bytes, device temporary bytes, peak host RSS and per-stage fixture walls. Build each rung's machine and exterior once and apply the three arms to it. The ladder's fixture cache under /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261009T160304793011-proto-ladder/map-rows/cache (machines at 500 and 2000 requested cells) may be read in place to skip rebuilding; do not write into it. If machine construction at 5,000 cells exceeds a 60-minute budget, run about 3,500 instead and name the binder with its stage wall.

(4) Orders. Give the fitted map order per arm and case where three rows exist, and the cell count at which each arm first meets relative sup 0.01.

(5) Figure. One SVG under docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/proto-support/: map relative sup against realised cells, log-log, one line per arm and case. Label each line directly, draw the 0.01 bound as a dotted grey line, and follow the repository data-ink plot style (no grid, despined, no title).

(6) Report. Write it at the assigned path, leading with the verdict: does the diverted map converge with refinement under the read arm, under the exact arm, or under neither; and where it does not, which term dominates the residual error (support, booking, exterior or discretisation).

Run conditions:
- All rows run in one H200 job: RECKON_ALLOW_NESTED_LAUNCH=1 sbatch --partition=betelgeuse --reservation=gpu_0003_grpA --gres=gpu:1, with --cpus-per-task 8 or more (up to 14 if admitted), --mem sized to what admits (group A carries mem=650G with 600G held by the serving lane, so read squeue a minute after submitting), and --time 03:00:00.
- XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false and TMPDIR=/tmp in the submit environment and in every child.
- On the compute node, run /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python directly with PYTHONPATH set to the run worktree; never invoke uv there. Every login-node uv command carries --no-sync, and nothing runs uv sync.
- Call configure_dtypes() before building any array, and assert jax_enable_x64.
- Declare any wait on the job as wait_probe ["sacct","-n","-X","-P","-j","(job id)","-o","State"] and wait_terminal ["COMPLETED","FAILED","CANCELLED","TIMEOUT","OUT_OF_MEMORY","NODE_FAIL"], as JSON lists.
- Commit with conventional subjects and bodies at every step. Write the manifest and commit before the job wait. The manifest commits line lists every commit. Status is complete, blocked or failed, which the worker sets itself.
